feature: Copy an edited video to the clipboard
summary: Edit > Copy Video and Copy as GIF put the whole edit on the clipboard as a file, cuts and burned-in captions included, so a trimmed recording pastes straight into a chat or the Finder without exporting first.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any screen recording.

try.do: Open a screen recording, put the playhead in the middle, press B on the clip and delete the second half.
Choose Edit > Copy Video (Control Shift Command C).
Watch the toast at the foot of the canvas fill, then read the pill that replaces it.
Paste into Messages or a Finder window and play what lands.
Choose Edit > Copy as GIF (Control Shift Command G) and paste it into a chat.
Open a screenshot instead and look at Edit: both rows are greyed out.

evaluate: Is Edit next to Copy where you would look for this, or did you reach for a right-click on the canvas or the clip first?
Are Control Shift Command C and G keys you would remember, or would you rather have one key and a choice in the toast?
Is the size and quality the Export sheet last used the right thing for a copy, or should a copy always be small enough for a chat?
Does the pill saying Copied plus the file name tell you enough to paste with confidence?
rough: No mock draws a clipboard copy for a video; the rows follow the placement contract (UX-PATTERNS menu bar and toasts rows) and add nothing anywhere else.
There is no right-click route yet: the canvas and clip menus do not offer Copy Video, so it is reachable only from Edit and its keys.
A copy uses whatever the Export sheet last chose for that format, so a person who last exported a Full size High MP4 copies a big file; nothing on the toast says which size it used.

A GIF at 15 frames a second plays about 5 percent long (4.0 s of edit plays 4.2 s), because GIF stores delays in hundredths; Export has the same behaviour and filed as a-gif-plays-at-the-speed-of-the-edit-it-came-fro.
While a copy writes, Export and a second copy are greyed out: one toast, one file at a time.
